runtimeGap: go vet and the combined targeted go test run could not complete on this host, and the cause is now measured rather than guessed. Any Go action that must make a fresh compiler/tool invocation blocks indefinitely: `go vet ./pkg/tenant/...` consumed 0.03s of user CPU across a 5-minute window and emitted no output, and `go vet -x` printed 345 `mkdir -p $WORK\...` lines and then blocked before invoking the compiler or the vet tool (vet.exe is present in GOROOT/pkg/tool). Three hypotheses were eliminated by experiment: it is not network (identical hang with GOPROXY=off, which would otherwise fail fast on a missing module), not test-file dependencies (identical with -tests=false), and not build-cache lock contention (reproduced with zero other Go processes running, immediately after a successful `go build`). Warm-cache operations succeed: `go build ./...` exits 0 in ~14s and `go list ./pkg/tenant/...` completes in 2.1s. Because go vet and go test always require a fresh compile/vet invocation, neither can complete here. Consequence: vet-specific checks and the two new regression tests' assertions remain unverified by execution this session; go build ./... passes, gofmt is clean, and the 34-assertion live probe exercises the same code paths end to end. Recorded as not-run rather than silently omitted.
